title: Algo gym
description: Classic algorithms and data structures in Python or C++: sort-and-sweep, monotonic stacks and deques, binary search on the answer, heaps, LRU caches, tries, union-find, BFS, Dijkstra, topological sort, minimum spanning trees, and dynamic programming. Every exercise has an editorial with the idea, the cost and the pitfalls. Hidden-size tests and time limits reward the right complexity, not just a right answer.

sources.title: CP-Algorithms
sources.note: Clear write-ups of union-find, Dijkstra, inversion counting and more.

sources.title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units (Sennrich et al., 2015)
sources.note: Byte-pair encoding, the algorithm in bpe_train.

sources.title: Introduction to Algorithms (Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest, Stein)
sources.note: Topological sort, Kruskal's algorithm and the cut property, BFS and dynamic programming.

tracks.name: Arrays and intervals
tracks.summary: Sorting, sweeping, monotonic stacks and deques, divide and conquer, and binary search on the answer.

tracks.name: Data structures
tracks.summary: Heaps, hash maps with linked lists, tries and sorted lists, union-find, and the pair counts that byte-pair encoding updates as it merges.

tracks.name: Graphs
tracks.summary: Breadth-first search, shortest paths with a heap, topological order, and minimum spanning trees.

tracks.name: Dynamic programming
tracks.summary: Tables over prefixes and budgets: edit distance, longest increasing subsequence and the 0/1 knapsack.
